title: Obtuse cosine in the 8-15-17 family
source: Theory P1-5.3 Quick check 3; 17s cos theta for an obtuse angle with sin=8/17
stem: Given that \(\sin\theta=\dfrac{{8}}{{17}}\) and that \(\theta\) is obtuse, find the value of \({hyp|int}\cos\theta\).

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The related adjacent side is \(15\times{s|int}\). Cosine is negative in the second quadrant, so \({hyp|int}\cos\theta={A|int}\).
steps.note: An 8-15-17 triangle, scaled by s, with cosine negative because the angle is obtuse.

title: Related-angle tangents and sine in terms of k

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The acute angle \(x\) radians is such that \(\tan x=k\), where \(k\) is a positive constant. Express, in terms of \(k\),

(i) \(\tan(\pi-x)\), [1]

(ii) \(\tan\bigl(\tfrac{{1}}{{2}}\pi-x\bigr)\), [1]

(iii) \(\sin x\). [2]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: B1, correct answer only.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: B1, correct answer only.

steps.name: s3
steps.text_tex: (iii) From a right-angled triangle, or from the identity \(1+\tan^2 x=\sec^2 x\), a method for \(\sin x\) is used.
steps.note: Official MS: M1, any valid method — a right-angled triangle or formulae.

title: Cosine, tangent and sine of an obtuse angle in terms of k

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
Given that \(\theta\) is an obtuse angle measured in radians and that \(\sin\theta=k\), find, in terms of \(k\), an expression for

(i) \(\cos\theta\), [1]

(ii) \(\tan\theta\), [2]

(iii) \(\sin(\theta+\pi)\). [1]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: B1, correct answer only.

steps.name: s2
steps.text_tex: (ii) \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{{\sin\theta}}{{\cos\theta}}\) is used, with an attempt at the cosine from (i).
steps.note: Official MS: M1. Used, attempt at cosine seen in (i).

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: A1, follow through their cosine as a function of k only, from part (i).

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: B1, correct answer only.

title: Sine and tangent of a reflex angle, and the sign of sine of twice the angle

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The reflex angle \(\theta\) is such that \(\cos\theta=k\), where \(0<k<1\).

(i) Find an expression, in terms of \(k\), for

(a) \(\sin\theta\), [2]

(b) \(\tan\theta\). [1]

(ii) Explain why \(\sin 2\theta\) is negative for \(0<k<1\). [2]

steps.name: s1
steps.text_tex: (i)(a) The minus sign: \(\sin\theta\) is negative because \(\theta\) is reflex (fourth quadrant).
steps.note: Official MS: B1 for the minus sign.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: B1 for the remaining expression.

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: B1, for (i) divided by k.

steps.name: s4
steps.text_tex: (ii) \(\theta\) is in the fourth quadrant, so \(2\theta\) lies between \(540^\circ\) and \(720^\circ\).
steps.note: Official MS: B1, correct answer only.

steps.name: s5
steps.text_tex: (ii) Sine is negative in both of those quadrants, so \(\sin 2\theta\) is negative.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, correct answer only.
